summary.headline: HCG Q1 FY27 revenue rose ~13% YoY to INR6,951 million on 11% volume growth; adjusted EBITDA up 20% to INR1,339 million, margin 19.4%.
summary.overview: Revenue reached INR6,951 million, up about 13% YoY, with volumes up 11% and ARPP up 2%. Adjusted EBITDA rose 20% YoY to INR1,339 million, with margin expanding to 19.4% from 18.2%, helped by a payor mix shift toward non-institutional business (69% vs 67%). The North Bangalore hospital, opened in May 2026, contributed INR67 million revenue and management says peak EBITDA loss was reached this quarter. A chemo drug discontinuation cost about 1.5% of top line but was margin-accretive.

segments.name: South cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue grew ~16% YoY on volume and realization growth, including North Bangalore's INR67 million; cash and TPA mix improving in Bangalore CoE and Vizag.

segments.name: West cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 9% YoY; Maharashtra grew over 14%, Gujarat moderate. Institutional business fell over 4% as low-margin scheme immunotherapy was cut; ARPP broadly stable.

segments.name: East cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 22% YoY on volume growth, despite temporary ARPP moderation.

segments.name: Hospital size buckets
segments.commentary: Hospitals above INR10 crore per month rose from 4 to 7; INR5-10 crore bucket fell from 14 to 11; below INR5 crore rose from 6 to 7 (including North Bangalore).

guidance_outlook: Mid-teens revenue growth outlook maintained for existing and new centres combined.
Long-term EBITDA margin: 21-22% within about 2 years; 24-25% over the next 4-5 years (management clarified 25% timeline in Q&A).

North Bangalore: peak EBITDA loss reached in Q1 FY27; losses expected to fall over the next few quarters; monthly breakeven expected this year; optimal 60-65% utilisation in 3rd-4th year of operation.
Chemo drug discontinuation to keep ~1.5% top-line impact for the next few quarters, may marginally decline.
ARPP growth expected in line with inflation.
Marketing spend to settle at 2.5-2.6% of revenue long term (2.9% currently).
ESOP charge to be quantified and reported in Q2 once policy is finalised.
Interest cost expected to moderate versus last year after INR170 crore debt repayment.
capex_capacity: 121 beds added in Q1 (South 61, West 27, East 26, Kenya 7).
Planned additions: 65 beds in FY27, 520 beds across FY28-FY29, 230 beds in FY30; ~60% brownfield.
Three greenfield projects in pipeline; two (~180 beds, Whitefield in South and a Maharashtra site in West) expected to operationalise around end-FY28 and the following year.
Commissioned a new LINAC in Rajkot (now a Comprehensive Cancer Centre); added two surgical robots (Nashik and Bangalore CoE replacement).
North Bangalore MR-LINAC commissioned in July 2026.
Existing facilities can run at 75-80% utilisation; Southern cluster was 68% in FY26.
demand_pricing: Volume growth of 11% drove the top line; ARPP up 2% helped by payor mix, offset by case mix shift away from high-value low-margin therapies.
Government/CGHS price capping cost about 1.5% of top line; margin impact not quantified.
Discontinued some high-value, low-margin chemo drugs (about 1.5% of Q1 revenue), which management says was margin-accretive.
Institutional business reduced about 200 bps of revenue mix; ~50% of centres are at 20%+ EBITDA margin.
North Bangalore: 550+ new patient registrations and 300+ admissions in its first quarter; onboarded about 20 oncologists in the last 4-5 months.
Sales and marketing spend up more than 20% YoY to about 2.9% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Growth in hospital revenue buckets and like-to-like growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Hospitals above INR10 crore/month rose from 4 to 7; like-to-like growth not disclosed and to be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for North Bangalore losses and ESOP charge?
qa_highlights.answer: Management believes peak EBITDA loss was reached in Q1; losses to fall over coming quarters. ESOP charge to be assessed and reported in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of drug discontinuation on FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: About 1.5% top-line impact in Q1, expected to stay in the same range for next few quarters; margin-accretive.

qa_highlights.question: Capex in Q1 and maintenance capex for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 capex about INR750 million (growth ~INR350 million, maintenance ~INR400 million per the call); FY27 maintenance capex about INR100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term EBITDA margin target and levers?
qa_highlights.answer: 21-22% in about 2 years, 24-25% in 4-5 years, driven by payor mix, clinical complexity, operating leverage and North Bangalore losses declining.

qa_highlights.question: Cash and use of rights issue proceeds?
qa_highlights.answer: Used INR170 crore for debt repayment, about INR150 crore to raise Vizag stake from 51% to 85%, and about INR95 crore for general corporate purposes per the call (figures as transcribed).

risks_watch: North Bangalore ramp-up: utilisation, insurance empanelment and loss trajectory; first-year losses still weigh on EBITDA.
Pricing pressure from CGHS/government price capping; ARPP up only 2% and management says top line could have been better.
Institutional business decline in West (over 4%) and Gujarat slowdown; watch replacement by cash/non-institutional patients.
ESOP charge impact on P&L, to be disclosed in Q2.
Margin target credibility: 24-25% EBITDA ambition depends on payor mix shift and operating leverage.
Management did not disclose cluster-level utilisation or like-to-like growth; disclosure limited to annual reporting.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins and volume momentum, but candid that top-line growth could have been better given price capping. Management was guarded on specifics, deferring cluster utilisation, like-to-like growth, CGHS margin impact and ARPP drivers to annual disclosure or offline follow-up.

financial_highlights.change: YoY; share 69% vs 67% in Q1 FY26
~INR350 million growth, ~INR400 million maintenance (as stated on call)

financial_highlights.metric: Operating cash flow before working capital

key_quotes: So I think as most of the costs have been built in, I feel we have reached the peak EBITDA loss in this quarter.

Our objective is not to only grow faster, but to grow with a better quality of earnings by treating more complex oncology cases, improving our patient mix, enhancing productivity and generating stronger returns on the capital we deploy.
I think we could have done better on both fronts, particularly on the top line, where we did face a couple of headwinds on the price capping and couple of those factors.
So I said in the next 2 years, we are looking at a 21%, 22% EBITDA margin. For the next 4 to 5 years, we are confident of clocking the 25% margin number.

adds.what: 65 beds planned in FY27 (121 beds added in Q1 FY27 already)
Whitefield (South) and Maharashtra (West) greenfield projects, ~180 beds combined

growth.why: Management reiterated mid-teens revenue growth (midpoint ~15%) with volumes up 11% and 121 beds added in Q1, backed by a bed pipeline of 65 in FY27 and 520 in FY28-29, though utilisation level was not quantified and the institutional business is shrinking.
